input.question: After World War 2 how did America end up with their economy improved and the rest of the world ended up broke?
input.ground_truth: America didn't get bombed and saw *immense* federal spending that ended the great depression. Also, as it turns out, being the only industrial power that didn't get bombed to hell makes your economy pretty strong as there isn't a whole lot of competition.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: After World War 2 how did America end up with their economy improved and the rest of the world ended up broke?

response.prediction:
Okay, imagine you and your friends are playing a big game together. You all have a lemonade stand, but then a huge storm (that’s like World War 2) comes and destroys everyone’s stands. Now, after the storm, your house (that’s like America) didn’t get as damaged as the other houses. You still have lots of lemons, sugar, and cups left. You can start selling lemonade again very quickly.

But your friends’ houses (that’s like other countries) got really hurt. They don’t have as many lemons or cups left, and it takes them a long time to fix their stands.

Now, here’s the special part: before the storm, your family sent lots of lemons and money to help your friends build their stands. But during and after the storm, your family actually helped fix things even more. They gave some of their lemons, sugar, and money to your friends to help them get back on their feet. Also, your family’s lemonade stand got even bigger because everyone wanted to buy from you since you had the most supplies.

At the same time, your friends had to use up all their lemons and money to fix their own houses and stands, so they didn’t have as much left to sell lemonade.

So, after the storm, your house (America) had lots of lemonade and money, while your friends’ houses (other countries) were still fixing their stands and didn’t have as much to sell.

That’s how America’s economy got better, and many other countries stayed poor for a while after World War 2.
